source.title: Sharpness-Aware Teleportation on Riemannian Manifolds
source.authors: Tuan Truong; Hoang-Phi Nguyen; Hao-Cheng Luo; Tung Pham; Mehrtash Harandi; Dinh Q. Phung; Trung Le

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some equations and table formatting are flattened, but the reported accuracy values can be assigned to their models, methods, and datasets.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares a new optimizer with existing optimizers and reports held-out classification accuracy, a different method and measure from the claim versions. It does not measure train-test gaps or test the listed version-specific conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out accuracy for RSAT and baseline optimizers. It does not report corresponding training error, so these results cannot establish the size of a training-test gap. Hessian spectra and parameter-perturbation robustness are not measures of the gap named in the claim. Prior-work results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study uses the premise that flatter minima improve generalization to design RSAT and reports its performance against other optimizers. It does not test any specified version: its sharpness measures are not magnitude-aware gap predictors, and its R-Adam results are quoted rather than measured in a controlled adaptive-versus-SGD experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they claim RSAT consistently outperforms their comparators and provide a population-loss bound involving worst-case empirical loss in a manifold neighborhood. This is their conclusion, not evidence that any listed version was tested.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Riemannian Sharpness-Aware Teleportation, combining a teleportation step with sharpness-aware optimization on a quotient manifold; experiments compare it with existing optimizers rather than reproducing the listed version methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture (ResNet34 versus ResNet50), and supervised versus unsupervised self-supervised setting change reported accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Across all eight Table 1 model–dataset settings, RSAT has higher reported linear-evaluation accuracy than SGD and R-SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RSAT improves linear-evaluation accuracy over these baselines in the tested SupCon vision settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6 reports lower Hessian maximum eigenvalue for RSAT than R-SAM on CIFAR100/ResNet34, 8.35 versus 13.93, and lower spectral ratio, 1.49 versus 3.05. Its separate perturbation experiment reports less accuracy degradation than SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RSAT can reduce Hessian curvature and improve robustness to unscaled gradient-direction parameter perturbations; these measurements do not establish V7's correlation with generalization gaps.

record.problems: No training errors or train-test gaps are reported alongside the accuracy results. The paper reports means with 95% confidence intervals across five runs for the image-classification tables, but Table 4 says R-Adam performance is directly quoted from another source.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports the same RSAT comparisons for ResNet34 and ResNet50 in the SimCLR setting across CIFAR100, CIFAR10, STL10, and Aircraft; these additional 16 rows are omitted to prioritize the labeled self-supervised setting. Tables 3 and 4 report additional cross-domain and SPD video-classification comparisons, but also lack training-error measurements. Table 5 runtime, Table 6 teleportation-solver comparisons, Hessian spectra, and parameter-perturbation robustness do not measure train-test gaps.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under controlled tuning, including broader tuning, weight decay and optimizer switching. Table 4 quotes R-Adam performance from another source.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes that remove those effects.
Dropout interventions, training-set size, excessive dropout and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus measured train-test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Missing training error is relevant to V7 but is not a universal reason to exclude accuracy comparisons from other versions. Here, the interventions and comparisons themselves do not match those versions. The theoretical bound concerns group-invariant manifold sharpness, not the empirical magnitude-aware ranking claim in V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
